title: La ruta equivocada
desc: The wrong bus, and an hour you do not get back
setting: You are standing in the door of a moving bus and the ayudante is looking at you.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.en: Get on, get on! Where are you going?

options.en: Does this route go through the centre?
options.feedback: Ask before your foot leaves the ground. He is shouting the route at every corner and he will tell you straight.
He now knows where you want to go. You still do not know whether this bus goes there.
You answered a question he did not ask and got on a bus nobody has checked.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: No, esta va para el otro lado. Bájese en la esquina.
steps.en: No, this one goes the other way. Get off at the corner.

options.en: Ah, ideay. And which bus do I take?
options.feedback: You took the mistake without fuss and asked the only useful question. He answers these forty times a day.

options.en: All right, I will get off.
options.feedback: You are off the wrong bus, which is progress. You are also on a corner you do not know.
Arguing with the ayudante costs you the corner he was going to point at.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: La 110. En la esquina de las frutas.

options.es: ¿En la esquina de las frutas? Ya. Gracias.
options.en: At the fruit corner? Right. Thanks.
options.feedback: You repeated the landmark back. Managua has no street names, so the landmark is the address.
Polite. Say the landmark out loud once and you will still have it in two minutes.
That was the address. The fruit lady is more use to you here than any street name.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.en: Off you go then. That is five pesos.

options.feedback: You pay on the way out, not on the way in, and joven is what you call a man his age.
You did not. On these buses the money changes hands when you get off.
It works. One word more and it would have sounded like you had done it before.
